title: Efficacy of CNN Architectures in Diagnosing Oral Cancer
author: Kulkarni, Sarwe, et al.

steps.title: Obtain original image dataset
steps.instruction: Collect the original histopathologic image set consisting of 1 224 images (both OSCC and normal cavity) as described in reference [21].

steps.title: Create augmented image set
steps.instruction: Use Keras ImageDataGenerator to generate an augmented dataset of 6 931 images from the original 1 224 images with the following transformations:

substeps.instruction: Apply random rotations uniformly sampled between 0° and 40°.
Apply random width and height translations up to 20 % of the image dimension.
Fill newly created pixels using the nearest‑pixel value.

steps.title: Confirm augmented dataset composition
steps.instruction: Verify that the augmented set contains the class‑wise image counts shown in Table 1:

substeps.instruction: 100× magnification – Normal: original 891 → after augmentation 780 (note: numbers as reported).

steps.title: Split data into training and test sets
steps.instruction: Randomly partition the 6 931 augmented images into 80 % for training (≈ 5 545 images) and 20 % for testing (≈ 1 386 images), preserving class proportions.

steps.title: Define CNN architectures
steps.instruction: Implement the five convolutional neural networks using the Keras framework:

steps.title: Customize pre‑trained models
steps.instruction: For VGG‑16, ResNet‑50 and Inception V3, replace the original top classification layers with custom fully‑connected layers appropriate for binary classification (normal vs OSCC) and then freeze all base convolutional layers before the first training phase.

steps.title: Train each model
steps.instruction: Train all five models on the training subset using the same augmentation pipeline, appropriate loss (binary cross‑entropy unless otherwise noted), optimizer, and number of epochs (details not specified in the source).

steps.title: Evaluate model performance
steps.instruction: After training, evaluate each model on the held‑out test set and record the following metrics:

substeps.instruction: Inception V3: Accuracy 51.86 %, Precision 1.29 %, Recall 99.21 %, F1‑Score 67.62 %.

steps.title: Record confusion matrices
steps.instruction: Generate 2 × 2 confusion matrices for each model using the test predictions:

substeps.instruction: VGG‑16: True Negatives 348, False Positives 359, False Negatives 309, True Positives 349.
ResNet‑50: True Negatives 579, False Positives 128, False Negatives 262, True Positives 396.
MobileNetV2: True Negatives 677, False Positives 30, False Negatives 74, True Positives 584.
Inception V3: True Negatives 8, False Positives 699, False Negatives 11, True Positives 647.

steps.title: Optional model refinements
steps.instruction: If further improvement is desired, apply any of the following strategies:

substeps.instruction: Balance the training dataset (e.g., oversample minority class).
Add additional custom fully‑connected layers to the top of VGG‑16 or other models.
Modify the loss function (e.g., use focal loss to address class imbalance).
Unfreeze more base layers and fine‑tune the entire network on the training data.
